newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up fresh demand.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps rose late afternoon on Wednesday on fresh regional demand as buyers emerge to pick up any aggressive offers in the physical market, traders said.
"The market is well supported at the $100 (per tonne) mark due to the upcoming summer demand in North Asia," one trader said.
Fuel oil was last quoted about 25 cents firmer from Tuesday at $101.50/$102.50, but well above this mornings low of $100.75/$101.75, brokers said.
Traders said the market also firmed due to the absence of large exports from the Middle East due high demand there for the summer season.
Market sentiment was also boosted by activites in the physical market where an offer on Tuesday at $101.50 per tonne free-on-board was quickly snapped up by a European major.
The physical market had traded to a high of $102.00 per tonne late last week and traders said that the fundamentals have not changed.
Gas oil swaps drifted in quiet trade on rangebound physical trading.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.00/$25.10 per barrel down from Tuesday's $25.35/$25.45, brokers said.
June traded in the morning at $25.05, they said.

Traders said the market lost some ground after June Brent closed 10 cents lower to $19.62 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange on Monday with further loses seen on Wednesday where it last traded down 41 cents.
Range bound physical trading also forced the swaps market to give up some of its early week gains.
Two 150,000 barrel cargoes traded on Tuesday at $25.20 per barrel and $25.40, both on free-on-board Singapore basis, both within the well defined $25.00-25.50 range.
Traders said there are about 150,000 tonnes of unsold prompt gas oil in Singapore which is keeping prices down.
As a result, the May/June swap spread is flat while the June/July spread has narrowed to about 15 cents compared to over 60 cents on Monday.
